items.description: 0G is a modular blockchain for AI, offering decentralized storage, data availability and compute for AI apps.
DoubleZero is a network of dedicated fiber links for blockchain validators, built to cut latency compared with the public internet, starting with Solana. 2Z pays contributors of bandwidth.

Aave is the largest decentralized lending protocol, letting users earn interest on deposits and borrow against crypto collateral across many blockchains. AAVE is used for governance and to backstop the protocol.
Fusionist is a sci-fi blockchain game studio whose ACE token is used across its games and the Endurance chain.
Cardano is a proof-of-stake blockchain developed with a research-first approach, with its protocols published in peer-reviewed papers. ADA is used for fees, staking and on-chain governance.
Aerodrome is the largest decentralized exchange on Coinbase's Base network, where AERO emissions are directed by locked-token voters to the pools they choose.
aixbt is an AI agent that posts crypto market analysis on X, built on Virtuals Protocol. AIXBT gives holders access to its analysis terminal.
Algorand is a proof-of-stake blockchain designed by MIT professor and Turing Award winner Silvio Micali, offering fast finality and low fees.
AltLayer is a protocol for launching custom rollups and restaked rollups. ALT is used for staking, governance and fees.
Animecoin is a token for anime fans, launched by Azuki on Arbitrum to power a community-owned anime ecosystem.
ApeCoin is a token tied to the Bored Ape Yacht Club NFT ecosystem, governed by the ApeCoin DAO and used across Yuga Labs projects and the ApeChain network.
ApeX Protocol is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures trading, backed by Bybit.

Aptos is a proof-of-stake blockchain built by former Meta engineers who worked on the Diem project. It uses the Move language and parallel execution for high throughput, and APT pays fees and secures the network.
Arweave is a decentralized storage network for keeping data permanently in exchange for a single upfront fee paid in AR.
Arbitrum is the largest Ethereum layer-2 network, using optimistic rollups to run Ethereum apps faster and cheaper. ARB governs the Arbitrum DAO.
Aster is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures and spot trading on BNB Chain and other networks, backed by YZi Labs. ASTER is its governance and rewards token.
Cosmos is a network of independent, interoperable blockchains connected by the IBC protocol. ATOM secures the Cosmos Hub through staking and is used for governance.

Avalanche is a smart contract platform built from a network of customizable blockchains, called L1s, that share a fast consensus protocol. AVAX pays fees and is staked by validators, and the network is used for DeFi and tokenized real-world assets.
Avantis is a decentralized exchange on Base for leveraged trading of crypto, forex and commodities. AVNT is its token.
Axie Infinity is a blockchain game where players collect and battle creatures called Axies. AXS is used for governance, staking and in-game purchases on the Ronin network.
Aztec is a privacy-focused Ethereum layer-2 network that lets developers build apps with private transactions and data.
Babylon lets bitcoin holders stake BTC to secure proof-of-stake networks without bridging or wrapping it. BABY is the token of the Babylon Genesis chain.
Banana Gun is a Telegram trading bot for sniping new tokens on Ethereum, Solana and other chains. BANANA holders receive a share of bot revenue.

Bitcoin Cash split from Bitcoin in 2017 in a dispute over how to scale the network. It uses larger blocks to allow more transactions at lower fees and keeps Bitcoin's 21 million coin cap and proof-of-work mining.
Berachain is an EVM blockchain that uses proof of liquidity, rewarding users who provide liquidity to its apps. BERA pays gas and is staked by validators.
Big Time is a free-to-play multiplayer action RPG where players earn the BIGTIME token and NFT items.
Bio Protocol funds and governs decentralized science projects through communities called BioDAOs, which back early-stage biotech research.
Blur is an NFT marketplace and aggregator for professional traders on Ethereum that also runs the Blend NFT lending protocol.

BNB is the native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain ecosystem started by Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange. It pays fees on BNB Smart Chain, gives discounts on Binance, and is regularly burned to reduce supply.
Book of Meme is a Solana memecoin that raised millions in a 2024 presale and aims to store memes permanently on decentralized storage.
Brett is a memecoin on Coinbase's Base network named after a character from Matt Furie's Boy's Club comic, Pepe's friend.
Bitcoin SV split from Bitcoin Cash in 2018, aiming to follow Satoshi Nakamoto's original vision with very large blocks for on-chain data and payments.

Bitcoin is the first decentralized cryptocurrency, created in 2009 by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto. A global network of miners secures its blockchain with proof of work, and its supply is capped at 21 million coins, which has made it the largest crypto asset and a store of value often called digital gold.
PancakeSwap is the largest decentralized exchange on BNB Chain and also runs on Ethereum and other networks. CAKE is used for governance and rewards.
Cash Cat is a cat-themed memecoin.
Canton Coin is the native token of the Canton Network, a blockchain built by Digital Asset for regulated financial institutions to tokenize and settle assets like bonds and repos with privacy.
Celo is a mobile-first, low-fee network for payments and stablecoins that moved from its own layer-1 to an Ethereum layer-2 in 2025.
Conflux is a layer-1 blockchain that is approved for use in China and combines proof of work with proof of stake.
CHIP is the token of USD.AI, a protocol that lends stablecoins against GPUs and other AI hardware to fund AI infrastructure.
Compound is one of the original DeFi lending protocols on Ethereum, letting users earn interest and borrow against crypto. COMP is its governance token.
Curve Finance is a decentralized exchange specialized in stablecoin and like-asset swaps with low slippage, and issues the crvUSD stablecoin. CRV is used for governance and fee sharing.
Dash, short for digital cash, is a payments-focused cryptocurrency that forked from Litecoin's code. Its masternode network enables instant transactions and optional privacy mixing.

Dogecoin started in 2013 as a joke based on the Shiba Inu doge meme and became one of the largest cryptocurrencies. It uses proof-of-work mining merged with Litecoin and has no supply cap, with about five billion new coins issued each year.
Polkadot connects multiple specialized blockchains that share security from a central relay chain. DOT is used for staking, governance and buying blockspace on the network.

dYdX is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures that runs on its own Cosmos-based blockchain, with a fully decentralized order book. DYDX is staked by validators and receives a share of trading fees.
Dymension is a blockchain for launching and connecting application-specific rollups called RollApps. DYM is used for staking and as the base asset across RollApps.
EigenLayer, now EigenCloud, lets ETH stakers restake their assets to secure other services in exchange for extra rewards. EIGEN is used for staking and to resolve disputes.
Ethena issues USDe, a synthetic dollar backed by crypto hedged with short perpetual futures, and the yield-bearing sUSDe. ENA is its governance token.
Ethereum Name Service lets users register human-readable names like alice.eth that point to wallet addresses and websites. ENS is its governance token.
Ethereum Classic is the original Ethereum chain, kept running by those who rejected the 2016 fork that reversed the DAO hack. It still uses proof-of-work mining and has a capped supply.

Ethereum is a programmable blockchain that runs smart contracts and hosts most of the world's decentralized finance, stablecoins, NFTs and tokenized assets. Ether is used to pay transaction fees and is staked to secure the network, which moved from proof of work to proof of stake in 2022.
ether.fi is a liquid staking and restaking protocol that issues eETH and weETH, and also offers a crypto credit card and cash account. ETHFI is its governance token.
Fartcoin is a Solana memecoin launched in October 2024 on the Pump.fun platform after an AI chatbot joked about the idea. It became one of the largest memecoins of the AI agent trend.
Artificial Superintelligence Alliance (FET) is the merged token of Fetch.ai, SingularityNET and Ocean Protocol, three projects building decentralized AI agents, marketplaces and data tools.
Filecoin is a decentralized storage network where providers earn FIL for storing data and proving it is still there over time.
Fogo is a high-speed blockchain built on Solana's Firedancer client and aimed at trading, with very fast block times.
GALA is the token of Gala Games, a platform for blockchain games, films and music.
GAS is the fee token of the Neo blockchain, distributed to NEO holders and used to pay for transactions and smart contracts.
GMT is the governance token of STEPN, a move-to-earn app that rewards users for walking and running with NFT sneakers.
GMX is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures and spot trading on Arbitrum and Avalanche, where liquidity providers act as the counterparty. GMX holders share in protocol fees.
Goatseus Maximus is a Solana memecoin made famous by Truth Terminal, an AI chatbot that promoted it, kicking off the AI agent memecoin trend in late 2024.

Gram, formerly Toncoin, is the native token of The Open Network (TON), a blockchain closely integrated with Telegram for payments, wallets and mini-apps. The project was originally designed by Telegram's founders.
Grass is a network where users share unused internet bandwidth through a browser extension so AI companies can collect public web data, earning GRASS in return.
Griffain is a Solana platform where users create AI agents that carry out on-chain tasks like trading and sending tokens.
Hedera is a public ledger governed by a council of large companies, using a hashgraph consensus algorithm instead of a traditional blockchain. HBAR pays fees and secures the network through staking.
Hemi is a network that combines Bitcoin and Ethereum, letting apps use native bitcoin in smart contracts. It was co-founded by early Bitcoin developer Jeff Garzik.
Hamster Kombat began as a viral tap-to-earn game on Telegram where players run a crypto exchange as a hamster CEO, and its token launched on TON in 2024.

Hyperliquid is a high-performance blockchain built around a fully on-chain order book for perpetual futures and spot trading, and it is the largest decentralized derivatives exchange. HYPE is used for staking, gas and fee discounts, and the protocol buys back HYPE with trading fees.
Hyperlane is a permissionless interoperability protocol that lets any blockchain send messages and tokens to any other. HYPER is used for staking and rewards.

The Internet Computer is a blockchain from the DFINITY Foundation that can host full web applications, data and AI models on-chain. ICP is used for governance and converted into cycles that pay for computation.
Immutable is a platform for blockchain games, with Immutable zkEVM and tools for player wallets and in-game asset trading.
Initia is a layer-1 blockchain built to host and connect a network of application-specific rollups called Interwoven Rollups. INIT is used for staking, gas and governance.
Injective is a layer-1 blockchain built for finance, with on-chain order books, derivatives and tokenized assets. INJ is used for fees, staking and weekly burn auctions.
io.net is a decentralized network that pools GPUs from data centers and individuals and rents them out for AI training and inference. IO pays suppliers and is used for staking.

Anthropic is an AI safety and research company organized as a public benefit corporation. It builds Claude, a family of large language models offered to consumers, developers and businesses through its apps, API and cloud partners including Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud.

The Roundhill Memory ETF invests in companies that make memory and storage chips, including DRAM, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and NAND flash makers, which have become a key bottleneck for AI hardware.

The iShares MSCI South Korea ETF holds large and mid-sized South Korean companies and is one of the most traded ways to invest in Korea's stock market. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix make up a large share of the fund, so it moves closely with the memory chip cycle.

GoPro makes action cameras, mounts and accessories, along with a subscription service for cloud backup and editing. Its HERO and MAX cameras are popular for sports, travel and video creators, and it sells through retailers and directly online.

IonQ builds quantum computers based on trapped-ion technology and sells access through its own cloud and the major public clouds. It has expanded into quantum networking and sensing through acquisitions including ID Quantique and Oxford Ionics.

Nebius Group builds and operates AI cloud infrastructure, renting out GPU clusters and software for training and running AI models. It emerged in 2024 from the restructuring of Yandex, after selling the Russian businesses, and also owns the data labeling firm Toloka and a stake in ClickHouse.

OpenAI is an artificial intelligence company organized as a public benefit corporation. It develops the GPT family of large language models and products built on them, including ChatGPT, the Sora video model and Codex coding agents, and sells API access to developers and enterprises. Microsoft is its largest outside shareholder.

Sandisk designs and makes NAND flash memory and storage products, including SSDs for data centers and PCs, memory cards and USB drives. It was spun off from Western Digital as an independent public company in February 2025 and makes its flash chips through a joint venture with Kioxia.

Tencent is one of China's largest technology companies. It runs WeChat and QQ, is the world's biggest video game publisher by revenue through studios like TiMi and stakes in Riot Games and Supercell, and has large payments, cloud, music and advertising businesses.
IOTA is a network designed for the Internet of Things and tokenized assets that charges no fees for basic transfers. It rebuilt its network on a Move-based proof-of-stake design in 2025.
Jito is the leading liquid staking and MEV infrastructure on Solana, issuing JitoSOL and running the block engine many validators use.
Jupiter is the largest swap aggregator on Solana, also offering perpetual futures, a launchpad and a mobile wallet. JUP is its governance token.

items.description: Kaito is an AI-powered crypto research platform that indexes social media and news, and runs Yaps, a leaderboard rewarding crypto commentary. KAITO is its token.
Kaspa is a proof-of-work cryptocurrency that uses the GHOSTDAG protocol to produce multiple blocks per second while staying decentralized.
Bonk is a dog-themed memecoin on Solana, airdropped to the Solana community in late 2022, and one of the network's best-known tokens. This market is quoted per 1,000 BONK.
Floki is a memecoin named after Elon Musk's Shiba Inu that has added a crypto education platform and a metaverse game. This market is quoted per 1,000 FLOKI.

Terra Classic is the original Terra blockchain, which collapsed in May 2022 when its UST stablecoin lost its peg. The community kept the chain running and burns LUNC through a transaction tax. This market is quoted per 1,000 LUNC.
Neiro is a memecoin named after the Shiba Inu adopted by the owner of Kabosu, the dog behind the Doge meme. This market is quoted per 1,000 NEIRO.
Pepe is a memecoin based on the Pepe the Frog meme, launched in 2023 with no team allocation or utility. This market is quoted per 1,000 PEPE.
Shiba Inu is a dog-themed memecoin launched as a Dogecoin rival that grew into an ecosystem with its own exchange and Shibarium layer-2 network. This market is quoted per 1,000 SHIB.
Solayer is a restaking protocol on Solana that is building a hardware-accelerated blockchain. LAYER is its governance and staking token.
Lido is the largest liquid staking protocol, letting users stake ETH and receive stETH that can be used in DeFi. LDO governs the Lido DAO.
Linea is an Ethereum layer-2 network built by Consensys, the company behind MetaMask, using zero-knowledge rollups. Its token burns part of network fees along with ETH.

Chainlink is the leading oracle network, feeding real-world data like prices into smart contracts. Its cross-chain protocol, CCIP, connects blockchains with each other and with traditional financial systems. LINK pays node operators and is staked to secure the service.
Lighter is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures that uses zero-knowledge proofs to verify order matching and offers zero-fee trading for retail users.
Litecoin is one of the oldest cryptocurrencies, created as a lighter, faster version of Bitcoin. It has a 2.5-minute block time, an 84 million coin cap and is widely used for payments.
Manta Network is an Ethereum layer-2 using zero-knowledge proofs for modular apps. MANTA is used for gas and governance.
Magic Eden is a multi-chain marketplace for NFTs and tokens, originally built on Solana. ME is its token for rewards and governance.
MegaETH is an Ethereum layer-2 network built for real-time performance, aiming for very high throughput and millisecond response times.
Official Melania Meme is a memecoin launched by Melania Trump in January 2025, shortly after the Official Trump token.
Memecoin (MEME) is the token of Memeland, a project from 9GAG, the online humor platform, aimed at web3 meme culture.
Merlin Chain is a Bitcoin layer-2 network that brings smart contracts and DeFi to Bitcoin assets such as BRC-20 tokens and Ordinals.
Meteora is a major liquidity protocol on Solana that runs dynamic pools used for trading and token launches.
Mina Protocol is a blockchain that stays a constant 22KB in size by using recursive zero-knowledge proofs, so anyone can verify the chain from a phone.

This market tracks the Russell 2000, an index of about 2,000 small US companies. It is the most widely used benchmark for small-cap stocks, which tend to be more sensitive to interest rates and the domestic economy than large caps.

The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed in the United States, weighted by market value. It covers about 80% of the US stock market's value and is the most widely followed benchmark for US stocks.
This market tracks the price of long-term US Treasury bonds. Bond prices move opposite to interest rates, so it tends to rise when Treasury yields fall and drop when they rise.

This market tracks the Nasdaq-100, an index of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange. It is dominated by tech giants like Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet and is often used as a benchmark for big tech.
Mantle is an Ethereum layer-2 network backed by Bybit's treasury. MNT is used for gas and governance.

Monad is a high-performance blockchain compatible with Ethereum's virtual machine that runs transactions in parallel to reach thousands of transactions per second. Its mainnet and MON token launched in November 2025.
Moo Deng is a Solana memecoin named after the viral baby pygmy hippo at Khao Kheow Open Zoo in Thailand.
Morpho is a decentralized lending protocol where anyone can create isolated lending markets, and it powers crypto-backed loans in apps like Coinbase. MORPHO is its governance token.
Movement is a network of blockchains that use the Move language, including an Ethereum layer-2. MOVE is used for gas, staking and governance.
NEAR Protocol is a sharded proof-of-stake blockchain focused on usability and AI applications, with features like named accounts and chain signatures for controlling assets on other chains.
Neo is one of the earliest smart contract platforms, launched in China in 2014 as Antshares. NEO is used for governance and generates GAS, which pays network fees.
Nillion is a network for private computation that lets apps store and process encrypted data without revealing it.
Notcoin started as a tap-to-earn game inside Telegram that drew tens of millions of players, and its token launched on the TON blockchain in 2024.
NEXPACE is the token of the MapleStory Universe, a blockchain ecosystem from Nexon built around its long-running MapleStory game, where in-game items can be owned and traded.
Ondo Finance tokenizes real-world assets such as US Treasuries and stocks, issuing products like USDY and OUSG and tokenized equities through Ondo Global Markets. ONDO is its governance token.
Optimism is an Ethereum layer-2 network and the creator of the OP Stack, the software behind a family of chains called the Superchain, including Coinbase's Base. OP is used for governance.
ORDI was the first BRC-20 token created on Bitcoin using the Ordinals protocol, which inscribes data onto individual satoshis.

This market tracks the yield on the 10-year US Treasury note, the most important interest rate in global finance. It underpins mortgage rates and corporate borrowing costs and reflects expectations for inflation, growth and Federal Reserve policy.
Applied Optoelectronics makes optical transceivers and lasers for data centers, along with equipment for cable TV broadband networks. Much of its manufacturing is in Texas, Taiwan and China.

Broadcom designs semiconductors for networking, wireless and storage, including the custom AI chips it builds for Google, Meta and others. It also owns a large infrastructure software business built through acquisitions such as VMware and CA Technologies.
Bitcoin dominance measures bitcoin's share of the total cryptocurrency market's value. It tends to rise when investors move into bitcoin as the safer bet and fall during altcoin rallies.
Ciena makes optical networking equipment and software used by telecom carriers, cloud providers and enterprises to move data over fiber, including high-speed links between AI data centers.
Cipher Mining runs large-scale bitcoin mining data centers in Texas and is converting part of its power capacity into hosting for AI and high-performance computing customers.

Coherent makes lasers, optical networking components and engineered materials. Its optical transceivers are used in data centers to connect AI clusters, and it also makes silicon carbide and industrial laser systems.
Credo Technology designs high-speed connectivity chips and active electrical cables that link servers and switches inside AI data centers.
CrowdStrike sells cloud-based cybersecurity software. Its Falcon platform protects laptops, servers, cloud workloads and identities from attacks and is used by most of the Fortune 500.

Corning makes specialty glass, ceramics and optical fiber. Its products include Gorilla Glass for phones, display glass for TVs, fiber optic cable for data centers and telecom networks, and pharmaceutical glass vials.

The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF holds North American software companies, including large names like Microsoft, Oracle, Salesforce and Palantir, and is a popular way to trade the software sector as a whole.

IREN, formerly Iris Energy, operates data centers powered by renewable energy. It started as a bitcoin miner and now rents out large Nvidia GPU clusters for AI, including under a multi-year contract with Microsoft.

Lam Research makes equipment used to manufacture semiconductors, specializing in etch and deposition tools. Its customers include the major memory and logic chipmakers such as TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron.

MercadoLibre runs Latin America's largest e-commerce marketplace and its fintech arm Mercado Pago, which offers payments, credit and digital banking. It operates across 18 countries, with Brazil, Mexico and Argentina as its largest markets, plus its own logistics network.

Cloudflare runs one of the world's largest networks, providing content delivery, DDoS protection, security and developer services. A large share of websites route traffic through it, and it also offers serverless computing and AI inference at the edge.
This market tracks the total value of cryptocurrencies outside the ten largest. It reflects demand for smaller, riskier altcoins, which tend to rally late in crypto bull markets.

Reddit runs a network of more than 100,000 online communities where users post, comment and vote on content. It makes money from advertising and from licensing its data to AI companies such as Google and OpenAI.
Super Micro Computer builds servers and storage systems, especially liquid-cooled racks packed with Nvidia GPUs for AI data centers.

SoFi Technologies is a digital bank offering student, personal and home loans, checking and savings accounts, investing and credit cards. It also sells banking software to other financial companies through its Galileo and Technisys platforms.
Seagate Technology is one of the world's largest makers of hard disk drives, with most sales going to cloud data centers. Its HAMR technology enables drives of 30TB and more.
Teradyne makes automated test equipment used to check semiconductors and electronics during manufacturing. It also owns Universal Robots, a maker of collaborative robot arms.
This market tracks the total value of all cryptocurrencies excluding bitcoin. It is a way to trade the altcoin market as a whole, led by Ethereum, XRP, BNB and Solana.

Take-Two Interactive is a video game publisher whose labels include Rockstar Games, maker of Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption, and 2K, which publishes NBA 2K, Civilization and BioShock. It also owns mobile publisher Zynga.
Unitree Robotics is a Chinese maker of legged robots, including quadruped robot dogs and low-cost humanoid robots such as the G1 and H1, sold to researchers, developers and businesses.
Vistra is one of the largest US power producers and electricity retailers. It runs a fleet of natural gas, nuclear, coal and solar plants, mainly in Texas, and is selling power to data centers.
PAX Gold is a token issued by Paxos where each token is backed by one troy ounce of London Good Delivery gold held in vaults. Its price follows the spot price of gold.
Pendle is a DeFi protocol that splits yield-bearing assets into principal and yield tokens, letting users lock in fixed yields or trade future yield.
PENGU is the token of Pudgy Penguins, one of the most popular NFT collections, which has expanded into toys, games and its own Abstract blockchain.

ConstitutionDAO was a 2021 crowdfunding effort that raised about $47 million in ether to try to buy an original copy of the US Constitution at auction. It lost, but its PEOPLE token kept trading as a memecoin.
Peanut the Squirrel is a Solana memecoin named after a pet squirrel seized and euthanized by New York officials in 2024, a story that went viral.
POL, formerly MATIC, is the token of Polygon, a network of Ethereum scaling solutions including the Polygon PoS chain and the AggLayer. It is used for fees and staking.
Polymesh is a blockchain built for regulated assets like security tokens, with identity and compliance built in.
Pons is a crypto token traded on Hyperliquid.
Popcat is a Solana memecoin based on the viral meme of a cat named Oatmeal popping its mouth open.
Succinct runs a decentralized network of provers that generate zero-knowledge proofs for blockchains and apps, built around its SP1 zkVM. PROVE pays provers and is staked to secure the network.

Pump.fun is a Solana platform for launching memecoins with a bonding curve, and it has been used to create millions of tokens. PUMP is its native token, sold in a large public sale in July 2025, and the platform uses revenue to buy it back.
Purr is a cat-themed memecoin and the first token launched on Hyperliquid's spot market, widely held by the Hyperliquid community.
Pyth Network is an oracle that delivers high-frequency price data from exchanges and trading firms to more than 100 blockchains.
Render Network connects artists and AI developers with people who have idle GPUs, paying node operators in RENDER for rendering and compute jobs.
Resolv is a protocol that issues USR, a dollar stablecoin backed by crypto collateral hedged with derivatives. RESOLV is its governance token.
Renzo is a liquid restaking protocol that lets users restake ETH through EigenLayer and receive a liquid token, ezETH. REZ is its governance token.
Reserve Rights backs the Reserve protocol, which lets anyone create asset-backed stablecoins and index tokens. RSR is staked as insurance.
THORChain is a decentralized exchange network that swaps native assets across blockchains, such as BTC for ETH, without wrapping. RUNE pairs with every asset in its pools.
Sonic is a high-speed EVM blockchain and the successor to Fantom. FTM holders swapped one-for-one into S, which is used for fees and staking.
Saga is a layer-1 protocol that lets developers launch dedicated blockchains, called Chainlets, especially for games and entertainment.
The Sandbox is a virtual world where players buy land, build games and trade creations as NFTs. SAND is used for purchases and governance.
Sei is a high-speed EVM blockchain built for trading, with parallel execution and fast finality.
Seeker is the token of the Solana Mobile ecosystem, built around the Seeker smartphone and its dApp store.
Sky is the rebranded MakerDAO, the protocol behind the DAI and USDS stablecoins, one of DeFi's oldest and largest lending systems. SKY replaced MKR as its governance token.
Synthetix is a DeFi protocol that provides liquidity for perpetual futures and synthetic assets. SNX is staked as collateral.

Solana is a high-throughput blockchain designed for fast, low-cost transactions. It is a major hub for decentralized trading, memecoins, payments and consumer apps, and SOL is used for fees and staking.
Sophon is a ZKsync-based layer-2 network focused on entertainment and consumer apps. SOPH is used for gas, staking and governance.

items.description: SPX6900 is a memecoin that parodies the S&P 500, joking that it will flip the stock market.
Stable is a blockchain built for USDT payments, backed by Bitfinex and Tether, where USDT is used as the gas token.
STBL is a stablecoin protocol that issues the USST stablecoin backed by tokenized real-world assets, separating principal from yield.
Starknet is an Ethereum layer-2 network that uses STARK zero-knowledge proofs and its own Cairo programming language. STRK is used for fees, staking and governance.
Stacks is a layer that brings smart contracts and DeFi to Bitcoin. Its sBTC lets bitcoin be used in Stacks apps, and STX holders can stack their tokens to earn BTC rewards.

Sui is a high-throughput proof-of-stake blockchain from Mysten Labs, founded by former Meta engineers. It uses the Move language and an object-based data model that lets many transactions run in parallel.
SuperVerse, formerly SuperFarm, builds NFT and gaming tools and communities, including the Impostors game.
SushiSwap is a decentralized exchange that began in 2020 as a fork of Uniswap and now operates across many chains.
Maple Finance is an on-chain lender that makes overcollateralized loans to institutions and offers yield through syrupUSDC and syrupUSDT. SYRUP is its governance and staking token.

Bittensor is a decentralized network that rewards contributors for producing machine intelligence, organized into specialized subnets for tasks like text generation, data scraping and model training. TAO has a 21 million supply cap.
Celestia is a modular blockchain that provides data availability for rollups and other chains, letting them post data cheaply. TIA is used for fees and staking.
Tensor is the leading NFT marketplace on Solana, built for active traders. TNSR is its governance token.
Tellor is a decentralized oracle network where reporters stake TRB to submit data on-chain.
Official Trump is a memecoin launched by Donald Trump days before his second inauguration in January 2025. Companies affiliated with Trump hold most of the supply, which unlocks over three years.
TRON is a blockchain known for hosting the largest share of USDT stablecoin transfers thanks to its low fees. TRX is used to pay for network resources and for staking.
Turbo is a memecoin created in 2023 by a digital artist who asked GPT-4 to design a cryptocurrency from scratch with a $69 budget.
UMA runs an optimistic oracle that settles real-world questions on-chain, used by prediction markets including Polymarket. UMA holders vote to resolve disputes.

Uniswap is the largest decentralized exchange, letting people swap tokens directly from their wallets through automated liquidity pools. UNI is its governance token, and the protocol has turned on fees that are used to buy back and burn UNI.
Useless Coin is a Solana memecoin that leans into having no utility at all, launched in 2025 on the Bonk.fun launchpad.
Usual issues USD0, a stablecoin backed by tokenized US Treasuries, and shares protocol revenue with USUAL token holders.
Virtuals Protocol is a platform on Base and Solana for creating and co-owning tokenized AI agents. VIRTUAL is the base currency for agent tokens on the platform.
Venice is a privacy-focused AI chat and API platform. Staking VVV gives free access to its AI API.
Wormhole is a cross-chain messaging protocol connecting more than 30 blockchains, used to move tokens and data between them. W is its governance token.
WalletConnect Token powers the WalletConnect Network, the protocol that links crypto wallets to apps through QR codes and deep links. WCT is used for staking, rewards and governance.
dogwifhat is a Solana memecoin featuring a Shiba Inu wearing a pink knit hat, which became one of the defining memecoins of 2024.

Worldcoin, now called World, is a project that verifies people are human by scanning their irises with a device called the Orb, giving each verified person a World ID and WLD tokens. It was co-founded by Sam Altman.
World Liberty Financial is a crypto project backed by the Trump family that issues the USD1 stablecoin. WLFI is its governance token and became tradable in September 2025.
Xai is an Arbitrum-based gaming blockchain from Ex Populus aimed at bringing traditional gamers to web3.
Stellar is a payment network for moving money across borders and issuing digital versions of currencies, including USDC. Lumens (XLM) pay small transaction fees and keep accounts active.
Monero is a privacy-focused cryptocurrency that hides senders, receivers and amounts by default using ring signatures and stealth addresses. It uses CPU-friendly proof-of-work mining.
Plasma is a blockchain built specifically for stablecoin payments, offering zero-fee USDT transfers and compatibility with Ethereum apps. XPL secures the network and pays for other transactions.

XRP is the native asset of the XRP Ledger, a blockchain built for fast, cheap payments and currency exchange. Ripple, the company behind much of its development, uses XRP for cross-border payment services and holds a large share of the supply.
Applied Optoelectronics makes optical transceivers and lasers for data centers, along with equipment for cable TV broadband networks. Much of its manufacturing is in Texas, Taiwan and China.

Apple designs consumer electronics and software, led by the iPhone, which makes up about half its revenue. It also sells Mac computers, iPads, Apple Watch, AirPods and Vision Pro, and has a fast-growing services business including the App Store, iCloud, Apple Music and Apple Pay.

Applied Materials is the largest maker of equipment used to manufacture semiconductors and displays. Its tools handle deposition, etch, ion implantation and inspection steps at fabs run by TSMC, Samsung, Intel and others.

Advanced Micro Devices designs processors and graphics chips for PCs, game consoles and data centers. Its EPYC server CPUs and Instinct AI accelerators compete with Intel and Nvidia, and its chips are made by TSMC.

Amazon is the world's largest online retailer and, through Amazon Web Services, the largest cloud computing provider. It also runs a major advertising business, Prime Video, Whole Foods, the Alexa assistant and the Kuiper satellite internet project.

Arm Holdings designs the processor architecture used in nearly every smartphone and a growing share of data center and PC chips. It licenses its designs to chipmakers like Apple, Qualcomm and Nvidia and earns royalties on each chip shipped. SoftBank owns most of the company.

ASML is a Dutch company that makes the lithography machines used to print chips. It is the only supplier of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems, which are essential for the most advanced processors made by TSMC, Samsung and Intel.

Broadcom designs semiconductors for networking, wireless and storage, including the custom AI chips it builds for Google, Meta and others. It also owns a large infrastructure software business built through acquisitions such as VMware and CA Technologies.

Alibaba Group runs China's largest e-commerce platforms, Taobao and Tmall, along with international marketplaces like AliExpress and Lazada. Its Alibaba Cloud is China's biggest cloud provider and develops the Qwen family of AI models.

BlackBerry, once a leading smartphone maker, now sells software. Its QNX operating system runs in hundreds of millions of vehicles and embedded devices, and it provides secure communications software to governments and enterprises.

Bloom Energy makes solid oxide fuel cells that generate electricity on-site from natural gas or hydrogen. Data centers, hospitals and manufacturers use its systems for reliable power without waiting for grid connections.
Allbirds makes shoes and apparel from natural and sustainable materials such as merino wool, eucalyptus fiber and sugarcane, and sells them online and through its stores and retail partners.

BitMine Immersion Technologies holds ether as its main treasury asset, making it one of the largest corporate holders of ETH. It started as a bitcoin mining and hosting company before pivoting to an ether treasury strategy in 2025.
RoboStrategy is a company that holds a portfolio of stakes in robotics and physical AI companies, offering public market exposure to a sector dominated by private firms.

Brent crude is the global benchmark for oil, used to price roughly two-thirds of the world's internationally traded crude. It is based on oil from North Sea fields and reacts to OPEC+ policy, geopolitics and global demand.

Blackstone is the world's largest alternative asset manager, with over $1 trillion in assets. It invests in private equity, real estate, credit, infrastructure and hedge funds on behalf of pension funds, insurers and wealthy individuals.
Cerebras Systems builds AI computers around its Wafer-Scale Engine, a single chip the size of a silicon wafer. It sells systems and runs a fast AI inference cloud used by developers and enterprises.

West Texas Intermediate (WTI) is the main benchmark for US crude oil. It is a light, sweet crude priced for delivery at Cushing, Oklahoma, and its price is driven by global supply, OPEC+ decisions, US production and economic growth.

Coinbase runs the largest US cryptocurrency exchange, serving retail and institutional customers. It also earns revenue from USDC stablecoin reserves, staking, custody for crypto ETFs, and its Base blockchain network.

Copper is the most widely used industrial metal for wiring, power grids, construction and electronics. Demand from electric vehicles, renewable energy and data centers has made it a bellwether for global growth.

Costco runs membership warehouse clubs that sell groceries, electronics, household goods and gas in bulk at low prices. It operates about 900 warehouses worldwide and earns much of its profit from membership fees.
Circle Internet Group issues USDC, the second-largest dollar stablecoin, and EURC. It earns most of its revenue from interest on the reserves backing USDC and went public on the NYSE in June 2025.
CrowdStrike sells cloud-based cybersecurity software. Its Falcon platform protects laptops, servers, cloud workloads and identities from attacks and is used by most of the Fortune 500.
CoreWeave is a cloud provider specializing in Nvidia GPU computing for AI. Its customers include Microsoft, OpenAI and Meta, and it went public on Nasdaq in March 2025.

ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) is China's largest maker of DRAM memory chips. Backed by the Hefei government and state funds, it supplies memory for PCs, phones and servers and is developing high-bandwidth memory.
Dell Technologies sells PCs, servers, storage and networking gear. Its AI server business, built around Nvidia GPUs, has become a major growth driver alongside its commercial laptops and desktops.

DraftKings runs online sports betting, iGaming and daily fantasy sports in North America. It operates in more than 25 US states and also owns the Golden Nugget Online Gaming and Jackpocket lottery apps.

The Roundhill Memory ETF invests in companies that make memory and storage chips, including DRAM, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and NAND flash makers, which have become a key bottleneck for AI hardware.

eBay runs one of the world's largest online marketplaces, connecting buyers and sellers in about 190 markets. It focuses on categories like collectibles, trading cards, auto parts, refurbished goods and luxury items.
The euro is the official currency of 20 European Union countries and the world's second most traded and held currency after the US dollar. EUR/USD is the most traded currency pair in the world.
The iShares MSCI Japan ETF holds large and mid-sized Japanese companies such as Toyota, Sony, Mitsubishi UFJ and Hitachi, giving broad exposure to Japan's stock market in US dollar terms.
The iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF holds large and mid-sized Taiwanese companies. TSMC is by far its biggest position, so the fund is heavily tied to the global semiconductor industry.

The iShares MSCI South Korea ETF holds large and mid-sized South Korean companies and is one of the most traded ways to invest in Korea's stock market. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix make up a large share of the fund, so it moves closely with the memory chip cycle.

The iShares MSCI Brazil ETF holds large and mid-sized Brazilian companies, led by oil producer Petrobras, miner Vale and the country's big banks. It is the most widely traded fund for Brazilian stocks.
The pound sterling is the currency of the United Kingdom and the oldest currency still in use. It is the fourth most traded currency, and GBP/USD, known as cable, is one of the major currency pairs.
GE Vernova makes gas turbines, wind turbines and electrical grid equipment, and services the power plants that use them. It was spun off from General Electric in April 2024.
GigaDevice Semiconductor is a Chinese chip designer that makes NOR flash memory, specialty DRAM and microcontrollers used in consumer electronics, cars and industrial equipment.

GameStop is a video game and collectibles retailer with stores in the US, Canada, Australia and Europe. It became the center of the 2021 meme-stock rally and has since cut costs, built a large cash position and added bitcoin to its balance sheet.

Gold is the world's most widely held precious metal and a traditional store of value. Investors and central banks buy it as a hedge against inflation, currency weakness and financial stress, and it is also used in jewelry and electronics.

Alphabet is the parent company of Google, which runs the world's most-used search engine, YouTube, Android, Chrome and Google Cloud. Most of its revenue comes from advertising. It develops the Gemini AI models and its own TPU chips, and also owns Waymo, the self-driving taxi company.
Hims & Hers Health is a telehealth company that sells prescription treatments online for hair loss, sexual health, dermatology, mental health and weight loss, delivered by subscription.

Robinhood Markets runs a commission-free trading app for stocks, options, crypto and futures. It also offers retirement accounts, a credit card, a Gold subscription and, after buying Bitstamp, a global crypto exchange.

Hyundai Motor Company is South Korea's largest automaker and, with its affiliate Kia, one of the world's biggest car groups by sales. It makes cars under the Hyundai and Genesis brands and is investing heavily in EVs, hydrogen vehicles and robotics through Boston Dynamics.
IBM sells hybrid cloud software, including Red Hat, along with consulting services, mainframe computers and AI tools under its watsonx brand. It is also a leader in quantum computing research.

Intel designs and makes processors for PCs and data centers, and is building a contract chipmaking business, Intel Foundry, to make chips for other companies. The US government and Nvidia both became major shareholders in 2025.

IREN, formerly Iris Energy, operates data centers powered by renewable energy. It started as a bitcoin miner and now rents out large Nvidia GPU clusters for AI, including under a multi-year contract with Microsoft.

The Nikkei 225 is Japan's best-known stock index, tracking 225 large companies listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Unlike most indices it is weighted by share price, so high-priced stocks like Fast Retailing and Tokyo Electron have an outsized effect.

The Japanese yen is the world's third most traded currency. It is often bought as a safe haven during market stress, and its value is heavily influenced by the gap between Japanese and US interest rates.

Kioxia is a Japanese maker of NAND flash memory and SSDs, formed from Toshiba's memory business. It co-invented NAND flash and produces chips jointly with Sandisk. It listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in December 2024.

The Direxion Daily South Korea Bull 3X Shares ETF aims to return three times the daily performance of the MSCI South Korea index. Because it resets daily, longer-term returns can differ sharply from three times the index.

The KOSPI 200 tracks 200 of the largest companies on the Korea Exchange and is South Korea's main benchmark for futures and options. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix make up a large share of the index.
Lumentum makes optical and photonic products, including lasers and transceivers that connect servers in AI data centers and components for telecom networks and 3D sensing.

Eli Lilly is a pharmaceutical company best known today for its GLP-1 drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound for diabetes and obesity. It also makes medicines for cancer, immunology and neuroscience, including the Alzheimer's treatment Kisunla.
The Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF invests in companies that make lasers, optical components and transceivers, the hardware that moves data at high speed between servers in AI data centers.
The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF holds equal weights of Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia, Meta and Tesla, the seven megacap tech stocks that have driven much of the US market's gains.

Meta Platforms owns Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, used by more than three billion people daily, and makes nearly all of its money from advertising. It is spending heavily on AI, including its Llama models, and on Reality Labs, which makes Quest headsets and Ray-Ban smart glasses.
MiniMax is a Chinese AI company that builds large language, video and voice models. Its consumer apps include the Talkie companion chatbot and the Hailuo video generator.

Moderna is a biotechnology company that develops medicines based on messenger RNA. It makes the Spikevax COVID-19 vaccine and the mRESVIA RSV vaccine, and is developing mRNA vaccines and therapies for flu, cancer and rare diseases.
Marvell Technology designs chips for data infrastructure, including custom AI accelerators for cloud companies, optical interconnect DSPs, networking switches and storage controllers.

Microsoft makes the Windows operating system, the Office productivity suite and the Azure cloud platform, the world's second-largest. It is a major investor in OpenAI and builds Copilot AI assistants across its products, and it also owns LinkedIn, GitHub and Xbox.

Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, is the largest corporate holder of bitcoin. It raises money through stock and debt offerings to buy more bitcoin, and still runs its original business intelligence software unit.

Micron Technology is one of the world's three largest makers of memory chips. It produces DRAM, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) used in AI accelerators, and NAND flash for data centers, PCs, phones and cars, with fabs in the US, Japan, Taiwan and Singapore.

Natural gas is used to generate electricity, heat homes and make industrial products. US prices are set at the Henry Hub in Louisiana and are known for big swings driven by weather, storage levels and LNG exports.

Nebius Group builds and operates AI cloud infrastructure, renting out GPU clusters and software for training and running AI models. It emerged in 2024 from the restructuring of Yandex, after selling the Russian businesses, and also owns the data labeling firm Toloka and a stake in ClickHouse.
The Roundhill Neocloud ETF invests in neoclouds, the new GPU cloud providers that rent out AI computing capacity, along with companies that supply them.

Cloudflare runs one of the world's largest networks, providing content delivery, DDoS protection, security and developer services. A large share of websites route traffic through it, and it also offers serverless computing and AI inference at the edge.

Netflix is the world's largest subscription streaming service, with more than 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries. It produces and licenses films and series, and has added an ad-supported plan, live events and games.
Nokia makes mobile network equipment, optical and IP networking gear, and licenses its large portfolio of wireless patents. It acquired optical networking company Infinera in 2025.
ServiceNow sells cloud software that automates IT, HR, customer service and other business workflows. Most large companies use its Now Platform, and it has added AI agents across its products.

Nvidia designs graphics processors and the AI accelerators that power most of the world's AI training and inference. Its data center business, built on GPUs, networking and the CUDA software platform, makes up the bulk of its revenue, alongside gaming, automotive and professional graphics.

Oracle sells database software, enterprise applications and cloud infrastructure. Its Oracle Cloud Infrastructure business has grown quickly on large AI computing contracts, including with OpenAI, alongside its long-running database and ERP businesses.

Palladium is a precious metal used mostly in catalytic converters for gasoline cars, where it cuts harmful emissions. Supply is concentrated in Russia and South Africa, which makes its price sensitive to sanctions and mine disruptions.

Platinum is a rare precious metal used mainly in catalytic converters for diesel vehicles, as well as in jewelry, chemical processing and hydrogen fuel cells. Most of the world's supply comes from South Africa.

Palantir Technologies builds data analytics software for governments and businesses. Its Gotham platform serves defense and intelligence agencies, Foundry is used by commercial customers, and its AIP platform helps organizations deploy AI models on their own data.

Qualcomm designs Snapdragon processors and modems used in most Android phones, and earns royalties on its large portfolio of wireless patents. It is expanding into PC chips, automotive platforms and data center AI.
Quantinuum builds trapped-ion quantum computers and quantum software. It was formed in 2021 by merging Honeywell Quantum Solutions with Cambridge Quantum, and Honeywell remains its majority owner.

Reddit runs a network of more than 100,000 online communities where users post, comment and vote on content. It makes money from advertising and from licensing its data to AI companies such as Google and OpenAI.

Rivian designs and builds electric vehicles, including the R1T pickup, R1S SUV and the smaller R2, plus electric delivery vans used by Amazon. It has a software and electronics joint venture with Volkswagen.

Rocket Lab builds and launches small rockets and makes satellites and spacecraft components. Its Electron rocket is one of the most-flown small launchers, and it is developing the larger, reusable Neutron rocket.
SharonAI provides GPU cloud computing for AI workloads from data centers in Australia and the United States, including high-density deployments of Nvidia hardware.

Shein is an online fast-fashion retailer that sells low-priced clothing, beauty and home goods in more than 150 countries. Its on-demand supply chain, built on thousands of contract manufacturers in China, lets it test small batches of new designs and scale up the winners.

Silver is both a precious metal and an industrial one. Around half of demand comes from industry, especially solar panels and electronics, with the rest from jewelry, silverware and investment, so its price swings more than gold's.

SK Hynix is a South Korean memory chipmaker and part of the SK Group. It is the world's second-largest DRAM maker and the leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI accelerators, and it also makes NAND flash through its Solidigm unit.

SK Hynix is a South Korean memory chipmaker and part of the SK Group. It is the world's second-largest DRAM maker and the leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI accelerators, and it also makes NAND flash through its Solidigm unit.

The VanEck Semiconductor ETF holds about 25 of the largest chip companies, weighted by market value, with Nvidia, TSMC and Broadcom as its biggest positions. It is one of the most popular ways to trade the semiconductor sector.

Samsung Electronics is the world's largest maker of memory chips and one of the biggest smartphone and TV makers. It also runs a contract chipmaking business and produces displays, home appliances and networking equipment.

Sandisk designs and makes NAND flash memory and storage products, including SSDs for data centers and PCs, memory cards and USB drives. It was spun off from Western Digital as an independent public company in February 2025 and makes its flash chips through a joint venture with Kioxia.

SoftBank Group is a Japanese investment holding company. It owns most of chip designer Arm, runs the Vision Fund tech investment funds, and has made large bets on AI, including major investments in OpenAI and the Stargate data center project.

The Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X Shares ETF aims to return three times the daily performance of an index of US-listed semiconductor companies. Because it resets daily, its returns over longer periods can differ sharply from three times the index.

The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed in the United States, weighted by market value. It covers about 80% of the US stock market's value and is the most widely followed benchmark for US stocks.

SpaceX designs, makes and launches rockets and spacecraft. Its reusable Falcon 9 dominates the global launch market, its Dragon capsule carries crew to the International Space Station, and its Starlink satellite network provides broadband internet worldwide. It is developing the fully reusable Starship.

Stretch (STRC) is a variable-rate perpetual preferred stock issued by Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin. It pays a monthly cash dividend that Strategy adjusts to keep the price near its $100 par value, and proceeds fund more bitcoin purchases.

Tesla designs and makes electric vehicles, including the Model 3, Model Y, Cybertruck and Semi, along with battery storage systems and solar products. It is also developing self-driving software, a robotaxi service and the Optimus humanoid robot.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) is the world's largest contract chipmaker. It manufactures the most advanced chips for Apple, Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm and others, and is expanding production with new fabs in Arizona, Japan and Germany.
Unitree Robotics is a Chinese maker of legged robots, including quadruped robot dogs and low-cost humanoid robots such as the G1 and H1, sold to researchers, developers and businesses.

The Sprott Uranium Miners ETF invests in companies that mine and explore for uranium, along with funds that hold physical uranium. Its price follows the uranium market, which is driven by demand from nuclear power plants.

USA Rare Earth is building a domestic supply chain for rare earth magnets, which are used in electric vehicles, wind turbines and defense systems. It is developing a magnet plant in Stillwater, Oklahoma and the Round Top rare earth deposit in Texas.
Western Digital makes hard disk drives, mainly high-capacity drives sold to cloud data centers. It spun off its flash memory business as Sandisk in 2025 to focus on HDDs.
The SPDR S&P Biotech ETF holds US biotechnology stocks in roughly equal weights, which gives smaller drug developers as much influence as large ones. It is a common gauge of sentiment toward biotech.
The Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund holds the energy companies in the S&P 500, led by Exxon Mobil and Chevron. It is the largest energy sector ETF and moves closely with oil and gas prices.

This market tracks the Nasdaq-100, an index of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange. It is dominated by tech giants like Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet and is often used as a benchmark for big tech.
Zhipu AI is a Chinese artificial intelligence company that develops the GLM family of large language models and the ChatGLM assistant. It spun out of Tsinghua University.
Zoom Communications makes the Zoom video meeting platform along with phone, chat, contact center and AI assistant products for businesses.
Yield Guild Games is a gaming guild and publisher that started by lending NFTs to players of blockchain games. YGG is its governance token.
Zcash is a privacy cryptocurrency that uses zero-knowledge proofs to let users shield transaction details. It shares Bitcoin's 21 million coin cap and halving schedule.
Horizen is a privacy-focused network that moved from its own proof-of-work chain to Base in 2025, offering privacy tools for apps.
ZetaChain is a layer-1 blockchain for building apps that work across many chains, including Bitcoin, from a single contract. ZETA is used for gas and staking.
ZKsync is an Ethereum layer-2 network that uses zero-knowledge proofs, built by Matter Labs. ZK is used for governance.
Zora is a social app and network on Base where every post can be minted and traded as a coin. ZORA is the platform's token.
LayerZero is an interoperability protocol that lets apps send messages and tokens across many blockchains. ZRO is its governance token.
